report.summary: Reviewed chunk 4 of gated_writes.py; enumerated docstring/comment claims, verified code paths, noted uncheckable cross-file claims and behavior details.
risks: promote_candidates docstring | medium | Claims 'Never raises' but code only catches PromotionUnavailable around the lock; _promote_locked can raise uncaught exceptions (e.g., from manager.create_worktree, _PinnedWorktreeGit, resolve_project, manager.cleanup_worktree before the try). To settle: trace all exception paths in _promote_locked and its callees within this file.

promote_candidates docstring | medium | Claims 'every failure mode ... is a refusal' but only lock acquisition failure is caught; failures within _promote_locked (worktree creation, git init, etc.) are not caught here and will propagate. To settle: inspect _promote_locked and helper functions for uncaught exceptions.

run_write_wave docstring | medium | Claims 'NEVER writes the primary checkout' but this chunk shows delegation to scheduler.dispatch for non-write tasks; whether that writes the primary checkout is outside this chunk. To settle: inspect scheduler.dispatch implementation.

run_write_wave docstring | medium | Claims 'never calls promote_candidates' but this chunk does not show the rest of the function; the claim is uncheckable from this window. To settle: inspect remaining lines of run_write_wave.

run_write_wave docstring | medium | Claims non-write tasks are delegated 'exactly as they would have run before this function existed' but this chunk shows dispatch(..., dry_run=False, parallel=False) without verifying that matches prior behavior. To settle: compare with prior dispatch call patterns.
run_write_wave docstring | medium | Claims 'cancel is forwarded to gate_candidates' but this chunk does not show the gate_candidates call; uncheckable. To settle: inspect rest of run_write_wave.

run_write_wave docstring | medium | Claims 'cancel=None is byte-identical to behaviour before cancel existed' but this chunk only shows the parameter default; cannot verify byte-identical behavior without full function. To settle: inspect full function and call sites.

_promote_locked cleanup | low | cleanup_worktree exceptions are recorded but reap_branches exceptions are swallowed silently; a reap failure could leave stale branches without any report. To settle: check if reap_branches failure is reported elsewhere.

_promote_one catch-all | low | Catches all exceptions and returns a refusal; but if the exception occurs after a partial promotion (e.g., after commit but before reset), the worktree may not be clean; the docstring claims _promote_one_inner resets on anticipated failures but not unanticipated ones. To settle: inspect _promote_one_inner to see if it resets on all exception paths.
promote_candidates filtering | low | Filters live candidates by id(c) not in live_ids; if a candidate is a proxy or wrapper, identity may not match; but candidates list is direct. Low risk.

AUTO_PROMOTE_LEVELS | low | Only 'never' is allowed; legacy values are coerced, but the docstring says 'legacy values cannot reach promote_candidates' -- this chunk shows coercion but not the call to promote_candidates; uncheckable.
run_write_wave length check | low | Raises RuntimeError if assignments length mismatches tasks; this is a check that can fail and is appropriate.
todos: Inspect remaining lines of run_write_wave to verify cancel forwarding, promote_candidates non-call, and primary checkout non-write.
Inspect _promote_one_inner to confirm worktree reset on all failure paths.
Inspect _promote_locked's exception paths (create_worktree, _PinnedWorktreeGit, resolve_project) for uncaught exceptions.
Verify scheduler.dispatch behavior for non-write tasks to confirm 'exactly as before' claim.
Check reap_branches failure handling for silent omission.

handoff.purpose: Promotion phase 2 and start of phase 3: promote_candidates, _promote_locked, _promote_one, governance verdict, and run_write_wave entry.

symbols.name: _promote_one
symbols.note: Wraps _promote_one_inner with a catch-all returning a refusal dict on any exception.

symbols.name: promote_candidates
symbols.note: Phase 2 entry: filters live candidates, acquires promotion lock, calls _promote_locked, returns report with not_gated.

symbols.name: _promote_locked
symbols.note: Creates integration worktree, pins git, resolves test command, promotes each candidate sequentially, cleans up worktree and branches.

symbols.name: AUTO_PROMOTE_LEVELS
symbols.note: Tuple containing only ('never',) to force auto_promote to never.

symbols.name: _governance_verdict
symbols.note: Calls daedalus.core.get_governance and returns (allowed, state, verdict); maps failures to ('unknown', headline).

symbols.name: run_write_wave
symbols.note: Phase 3 entry: validates assignments length, coerces auto_promote, dispatches non-write tasks, then processes write tasks (continues beyond chunk).

claims.text: ``_promote_one_inner``, with a catch-all so ONE candidate's unexpected failure ... reports as a refusal rather than aborting the whole promotion batch.
claims.why: The function wraps _promote_one_inner in try/except Exception and returns a refusal dict with 'promoted': False, so one candidate's failure is contained.

claims.text: ``_promote_one_inner`` already resets the integration worktree to ``current_head`` on any failure it anticipates; this is the net under that for the failures it does not.
claims.why: The claim about _promote_one_inner's behavior is outside this chunk; this chunk only shows the catch-all wrapper.

claims.text: PHASE 2 -- see module docstring for the full argument. NOT called automatically by anything in this module or by ``KairosScheduler``; an explicit, separate call.
claims.why: The chunk does not show call sites elsewhere in the module or scheduler; cannot verify the claim from this window.

claims.text: ``candidates`` is what Phase 1 (``gate_candidates``) returned, in the SAME order they were submitted -- that order is promotion order too
claims.why: The chunk does not show gate_candidates or the call site that passes candidates; order preservation is not observable here.

claims.text: Never raises: every failure mode (lock unavailable, apply refused, cumulative gate failed, base moved and the retry also failed) is a refusal in the returned report, not an exception.
claims.why: The function only catches PromotionUnavailable around the lock; _promote_locked is called inside the try but its exceptions (e.g., from manager.create_worktree, _PinnedWorktreeGit, resolve_project) are not caught here and will propagate, violating 'never raises'.

claims.text: ``cancel`` is forwarded to every STALENESS-triggered regeneration (``_reattempt``'s own ``TaskAttempt`` ...) AND to the cumulative re-gate's own ``command_gate`` call inside ``_promote_one_inner``
claims.why: The chunk shows cancel being passed to _promote_locked, but the forwarding to _reattempt and _promote_one_inner is not visible in this chunk.

claims.text: A cancellation landing there is reported distinctly (``_CumulativeGateCancelled`` in the refusal ``reason``, never conflated with an ordinary ``cumulative gate failed``)
claims.why: The handling of _CumulativeGateCancelled is in _promote_one_inner, not shown in this chunk.

claims.text: the SAME unconditional ``git reset --hard``/``clean -fd`` that already runs for a genuine cumulative-gate failure also runs for a cancelled one
claims.why: The reset/clean logic is in _promote_one_inner, not visible in this chunk.

claims.text: honouring ``cancel`` here does not add a new way to leave the integration worktree in a worse state than finishing would; it only shortens how long a stop request takes to land.
claims.why: Depends on the cancellation handling in _promote_one_inner and _reattempt, not visible here.

claims.text: Reported, not dropped: a candidate that never reached STATE_CLEAN in Phase 1 ... has nothing to promote, but silently omitting it here would make this report LOOK complete ... Filtered by object IDENTITY, not dataclass equality
claims.why: The code builds not_gated from candidates whose id(c) is not in live_ids, and includes them in the report; identity filtering is exactly as described.

claims.text: if ledger_path is None: ... resolve_spine_db_path ... if ledger_error or ledger_path is None: ... refused with 'ledger unavailable'
claims.why: The code imports resolve_spine_db_path, calls it, and returns a refusal dict with reason 'ledger unavailable: {ledger_error}' when ledger_error or ledger_path is None.

claims.text: with _PromotionLock ... except PromotionUnavailable as e: ... report = refusal dict with reason str(e)
claims.why: The code catches PromotionUnavailable and builds a refusal report for each live candidate with the exception message.

claims.text: integration worktree has no readable gitdir pointer; refusing to promote into it unpinned
claims.why: The code checks if git.admin_dir is None and returns a refusal dict with that exact reason for all live candidates.

claims.text: no file in the primary checkout was changed; nothing is merged until a human (or a separately-invoked step) acts on the integration branch above
claims.why: The report includes that exact note; the code only operates on the integration worktree, not the primary checkout.

claims.text: ``auto_promote`` remains in the call signature so saved build sessions and third-party callers fail closed instead of crashing during migration. The only production-capable value is 'never'; legacy values cannot reach ``promote_candidates``.
claims.why: The chunk shows AUTO_PROMOTE_LEVELS = ('never',) and coercion in run_write_wave, but does not show the call to promote_candidates or the migration path; cannot verify legacy values cannot reach it.

claims.text: ``(promotion_allowed, governance_state, headline)`` -- read straight off ``daedalus.core.get_governance``, never re-derived here.
claims.why: The function imports get_governance and returns values derived directly from its result.

claims.text: That function's own docstring is explicit that a SECOND opinion on ``promotion_allowed`` is how an override sneaks in ... this module composes with it by calling it, not by re-implementing the discrimination check.
claims.why: The docstring of daedalus.core.get_governance is not in this chunk; cannot verify the claim about its content.

claims.text: Any failure to even ASK the question -- ``daedalus.core`` unimportable, the call itself raising -- reports the vocabulary's ``unknown``, not a silent True.
claims.why: Both import and call are wrapped in try/except Exception and return False, 'unknown', with an error headline.

claims.text: ``unknown`` and ``absent`` stay distinct facts ... this only ever manufactures ``unknown`` for a failure that happened HERE; a real ``absent`` receipt is already reported correctly by ``get_governance`` itself and passes through unchanged.
claims.why: The code passes through gov.get('state') or 'unknown', but the distinction between 'unknown' and 'absent' depends on get_governance's return values, which are not visible in this chunk.

claims.text: ``cancel``, when given, is forwarded to ``gate_candidates`` for every concurrent attempt in this wave.
claims.why: The chunk does not show the gate_candidates call; it only shows the beginning of run_write_wave.

claims.text: ``None`` (the default) is byte-identical to this function's behaviour before ``cancel`` existed: no caller that does not pass it is affected.
claims.why: The chunk does not show the full function behavior; cannot verify byte-identical behavior without the rest of the function and previous versions.

claims.text: A caller driving a longer-lived loop ... can pass one shared token/``KillSwitch`` here so a stop request reaches every in-flight ``TaskAttempt`` and every in-flight cumulative gate this wave started, cooperatively, instead of relying solely on the killswitch's process-wide sweep (which still works today with ``cancel=None`` ... but can race a gate's own poll and report a fabricated verdict; that race is exactly what this parameter exists to close).
claims.why: The forwarding to gate_candidates and the race explanation depend on code outside this chunk; cannot verify.

claims.text: ``assignments`` MUST be ``scheduler.accept(tasks, repo_root=repo_root)``'s own return, in the SAME order as ``tasks`` -- the caller (``WaveExecutor.run_wave``) already computed this ... Recomputing it here would still be SAFE ... but would silently trust two call sites to keep agreeing forever ... Passed in once, length-checked, used once.
claims.why: The function checks len(assignments) == len(tasks) and raises RuntimeError otherwise; it uses assignments as provided and does not recompute accept.

claims.text: Returns one result dict per entry in ``tasks``, position-matched -- the same contract ``KairosScheduler.dispatch`` already gives ``WaveExecutor.run_wave`` (see that method's length check immediately after this call).
claims.why: The chunk shows results list initialized to None and non-write tasks filled positionally, but the write-task results are filled in code not shown; also the reference to KairosScheduler.dispatch is external.

claims.text: Non-write tasks in the SAME wave (advisory, or bounced to the senior lane) are NOT touched by the gated path: they are delegated back to ``scheduler.dispatch``, scoped to just their own indices, exactly as they would have run before this function existed.
claims.why: The code builds other_idx, extracts other_tasks, calls scheduler.dispatch on them, and places results back at the original indices.

claims.text: NEVER writes the primary checkout and never calls ``promote_candidates``.
claims.why: The chunk shows only the beginning of run_write_wave; the rest of the function (which likely calls gate_candidates) is not shown, so we cannot verify it never calls promote_candidates or writes the primary checkout.

claims.why: The code coerces auto_promote to 'never' if not in AUTO_PROMOTE_LEVELS, but the 'reported as denied input' part is not visible in this chunk (likely in the rest of the function).

observations.what: promote_candidates claims 'Never raises' but only catches PromotionUnavailable; exceptions from _promote_locked propagate.
_promote_locked performs repository mutations (create_worktree, reset/clean in _promote_one_inner, cleanup) and is called inside the lock.
run_write_wave delegates non-write tasks to scheduler.dispatch with dry_run=False, parallel=False; this may write to the primary checkout depending on dispatch implementation.
The docstring claims run_write_wave never calls promote_candidates, but the rest of the function is not shown; the claim is uncheckable.
AUTO_PROMOTE_LEVELS only contains 'never'; legacy values are coerced but not reported as denied in this chunk.
_promote_locked swallows reap_branches exceptions silently, which could leave stale branches unreported.
